content:
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data Scientist with experience building and evaluating forecasting, churn and experimentation solutions using Python, SQL and cloud data tools. Delivered measurable improvements through a recipe-demand forecasting workflow and churn-targeting analysis. Experienced in feature engineering, scheduled notebook workflows, batch scoring, BigQuery, and automated tests for forecasting feature code. MSc in Statistics, with a strong foundation in modelling and experimental design.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and analysis: Python, SQL, R
Machine learning: LightGBM, XGBoost, scikit-learn, feature engineering, SHAP, forecasting, churn modelling
Data and cloud tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Looker
Engineering and experimentation: pytest, unit testing, Docker, Streamlit, statsmodels, R Markdown, sequential A/B testing
Additional learning: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox | 2022–Present
- Built a six-week-ahead weekly recipe-demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM, with calendar, price and menu-position features.
- Ran forecasts as scheduled notebook jobs in Vertex AI Workbench, writing results to BigQuery for operations reporting in Looker.
- Improved forecast WAPE from 23% to 14%; estimated food waste reduction was 9%.
- Developed a weekly XGBoost churn-scoring workflow in BigQuery to identify top-decile customers for retention offers.
- Validated retention targeting using a 10% holdout; churn decreased by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.
- Wrote a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, used by approximately 25 people in product and growth. Wrote its Dockerfile; the data platform team handled deployment to Cloud Run.
- Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
- Delivered the internal training session “Stats for PMs” three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | 2020–2022
- Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

EDUCATION
MSc in Statistics
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models

ADDITIONAL PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep-learning course, achieving approximately 80% accuracy.
- Tools: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It uses strong quantified outcomes, including the WAPE reduction from 23% to 14%, estimated 9% food-waste reduction, 2.1-percentage-point churn reduction, and adoption of the Streamlit application by approximately 25 users. The experience bullets are specific and generally distinguish the candidate’s work from platform-team responsibilities, which supports credibility. The main content limitation is that the document presents a strong data-science profile but does not clearly frame the transition toward machine learning engineering. It also gives limited detail about software-engineering practices, orchestration, and operational ownership—important areas for this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The simple section headings, reverse-chronological structure, standard bullet formatting, and text-based content should parse well in most ATS platforms. Relevant keywords such as Python, SQL, LightGBM, XGBoost, scikit-learn, feature engineering, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, Streamlit, pytest, batch scoring, and forecasting are present. However, the document has a relatively low-to-moderate AI screening probability for this particular vacancy because it does not include supported terms such as `dbt Cloud Scheduler`, `orchestration`, `model serving`, `monitoring`, `data versioning`, `LLM`, `chat assistant`, or `RAG`; most of these are genuine gaps rather than keywords that should be added. The `[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]` placeholders should be replaced with actual contact details before submission. The `Additional learning` section is appropriately separated from core experience, which avoids overstating PyTorch knowledge.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with forecasting, churn modelling, experimentation, feature engineering, Python, GCP data services, batch scoring, and measurable business impact. It also demonstrates some relevant engineering foundations through Docker, pytest, scheduled notebook jobs, BigQuery, dbt, and a Streamlit application used by product and growth teams. The candidate’s MSc in Statistics is relevant to modelling and experimentation but does not exactly match the advertised degree areas of machine learning, computer science, or engineering. The candidate material does not show at least four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production; the documented work is as a Data Scientist, with scheduled notebook and batch-scoring workflows rather than self-managed model APIs. The material also does not show chat assistants or RAG, production model serving, monitoring, or data versioning. Experience with a major cloud provider is shown through BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, but not broader GCP infrastructure ownership. Strong Python is supported by the forecasting, churn, Streamlit, and testing work. The candidate has orchestration-related experience through scheduled notebooks and dbt Cloud Scheduler, but the CV does not name dbt Cloud Scheduler. Feature engineering is shown; a distinct data-ingestion-pipeline experience is not shown. The document demonstrates practical problem-solving, ownership of analytical products, internal knowledge sharing, and collaboration with product, growth, operations, and platform teams, but it does not explicitly evidence all of the company’s culture signals.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CV CHANGES:
1. In the Professional Summary, change the opening to accurately position the transition without claiming MLE experience, for example: `Data Scientist transitioning into Machine Learning Engineering, with experience building, evaluating, and operating scheduled forecasting and batch-scoring workflows using Python, SQL, BigQuery, and Vertex AI Workbench.` Retain the quantified outcomes and add that the work includes feature engineering, orchestration through scheduled jobs, Docker, and pytest. Do not describe the candidate as having shipped model APIs or production AI assistants.

2. In the Technical Skills section under `Data and cloud tools`, change `dbt` to `dbt, dbt Cloud Scheduler` because the candidate’s notes specifically support use of dbt Cloud Scheduler. Add `orchestration: scheduled notebook jobs, dbt Cloud Scheduler` as a separate line or category. This improves alignment with the orchestration requirement without claiming experience with Airflow, MLflow, Kubeflow, or Kubernetes.

3. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the forecasting workflow bullets to make the operational lifecycle more ATS-readable while remaining accurate. For example, change `Ran forecasts as scheduled notebook jobs in Vertex AI Workbench, writing results to BigQuery for operations reporting in Looker.` to `Orchestrated weekly batch forecasting through scheduled notebook jobs in Vertex AI Workbench; wrote forecast outputs to BigQuery for operational reporting in Looker.` This accurately surfaces `orchestration`, `batch`, and the GCP services used.

4. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the churn bullet to state the data workflow more explicitly: `Developed and ran a weekly XGBoost churn-scoring workflow in BigQuery, using engineered customer features to batch-score customers and identify the top decile for retention offers.` Only retain `data pipeline` or `data ingestion pipeline` terminology if the candidate actually performed those activities; the supplied material does not establish that.

5. In the Streamlit project bullet, preserve the current deployment boundary but make the software-engineering contribution more searchable: `Built and containerised a Streamlit application in Python for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests; wrote the Dockerfile, while the data platform team deployed it to Cloud Run.` This is more precise than implying personal ownership of Cloud Run deployment.

6. In the pytest bullet, change `Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.` to `Added pytest unit tests for forecasting feature-engineering code in 2025, reaching approximately 60% test coverage.` This presents the contribution more directly and adds the supported `feature-engineering` keyword.

7. In the Professional Summary or Technical Skills section, explicitly name the cloud scope as `GCP services: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench` rather than presenting broad GCP infrastructure expertise. This improves ATS matching while remaining consistent with the candidate’s note that they cannot claim wider GCP infrastructure knowledge.

MINOR / ATS AND PRESENTATION CHANGES:
8. Replace `[EMAIL]`, `[PHONE]`, and `[LINKEDIN]` in the header with the actual contact details before submitting. Keep the header as plain text and avoid icons, tables, text boxes, or graphics.

9. In the `Additional learning` section, change the heading to `Additional Training and Projects` or retain the current heading but keep the words `course project` visible beside PyTorch. This makes clear that PyTorch and torchvision are learning-project experience rather than professional production experience.

10. Add a short `Selected ML Projects` label before the forecasting, churn, or experimentation achievements only if the CV layout needs clearer project grouping; otherwise retain them under professional experience. Do not create claims about model serving, monitoring, data versioning, chat assistants, RAG, or LLMs because those capabilities are not supported by the candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional and unusually clear about the candidate’s actual level of production experience. The strongest evidence is quantified: WAPE improved from 23% to 14%, estimated food waste reduction was 9%, churn decreased by 2.1 percentage points, and the Streamlit tool was used by approximately 25 people. The progression from analyst to data scientist is easy to follow, and the CV presents relevant engineering-adjacent experience without overstating API deployment or cloud infrastructure ownership. The main content limitation is role fit: the document demonstrates data science, scheduled batch workflows, feature engineering and early software-engineering practice, but not the central customer-support AI, language-model, model-serving or production MLOps experience required by this vacancy. The contact placeholders also make the document incomplete for submission.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly section headings, standard bullet points, conventional chronology and searchable technology names such as Python, SQL, GCP, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, pytest, LightGBM and XGBoost. It should parse well overall. ATS alignment is weakened by the absence of several job-specific terms that the candidate’s material does not support, including chat assistants, RAG, language models, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow and production API deployment; these must not be added merely to match the advertisement. AI screening probability is moderate to low for this specific role: the CV will likely pass basic parsing, but automated ranking may reject it because several must-have requirements are genuine experience gaps rather than wording deficiencies.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: This is a truthful and credible CV for a data scientist moving toward a junior or mid-level machine learning engineering role, but it is only a partial match for this vacancy. Strong matches include Python, GCP usage through BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, feature engineering, scheduled orchestration, batch scoring, Docker, pytest, automated testing and measurable ML outcomes. The CV also shows practical ownership of workflows and collaboration with a data platform team, which supports the company’s ownership and practical problem-solving themes. However, the candidate material does not show four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production; it shows data scientist experience with scheduled notebook forecasting and SQL batch scoring. It does not show chat assistants, RAG, language-model work, production model serving, monitoring, data versioning or the named MLOps platforms. The MSc in Statistics is relevant to modelling but is not a degree in machine learning, computer science or an engineering field. The document should therefore position the candidate’s strongest adjacent evidence accurately rather than imply full fulfilment of the role’s production-AI requirements.

It also demonstrates ownership, practical delivery, measurable outcomes, internal knowledge sharing, and collaboration with a data platform team, which align reasonably with Quillstone's pragmatic, learning-oriented culture. However, the candidate's material shows substantial role-alignment gaps: the candidate has not built chat assistants or RAG systems; has not fine-tuned language models; has not independently deployed a model as an API; has no stated monitoring or data-versioning experience; has no MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, or LLM-observability experience; and has not completed four years as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production. The available evidence supports scheduled notebook forecasting and weekly SQL/batch scoring rather than the full production-serving scope of this vacancy. The MSc in Statistics is relevant to modelling and experimentation but is not a degree in machine learning, computer science, or engineering.

The current use of “Cloud: GCP — BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench; dbt, dbt Cloud Scheduler, Looker” is parseable but could be made more precise by separating cloud services, analytics tools, and orchestration tools.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with Python-based ML workflows, feature engineering, GCP, scheduled orchestration, batch scoring, experimentation, automated testing, and measurable business impact. The MSc in Statistics is a relevant quantitative degree, although it is not a machine learning, computer science, or engineering degree. The candidate has approximately four years of data-science experience, but the material does not establish four years as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production. The forecasting and churn systems are scheduled notebook and BigQuery batch workflows rather than model-serving APIs. The candidate's material also shows no experience with chat assistants, RAG, large text datasets, language-model fine-tuning, monitoring, data versioning, or the named MLOps platforms. These are substantive job-alignment gaps, not CV-writing defects. The document does align with the company's practical, ownership-oriented culture through quantified operational delivery, cross-functional use of tools, internal training, and testing, but it does not explicitly provide evidence related to several culture signals such as candid feedback or team autonomy.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES:
1. In the Technical Skills section, replace the combined line “Cloud: GCP — BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench; dbt, dbt Cloud Scheduler, Looker” with separate, more precise lines: “Cloud and data platforms: GCP, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench” and “Analytics and orchestration: dbt, dbt Cloud Scheduler, Looker, scheduled notebook jobs.” This improves ATS parsing and avoids implying that dbt and Looker are GCP services.
2. In the Professional Summary, make the production scope more explicit rather than using the broad phrase “operating scheduled forecasting and batch-scoring workflows.” For example, change it to: “Data Scientist transitioning into Machine Learning Engineering, with experience building and operating scheduled forecasting and batch-scoring workflows in Python and SQL on GCP. Delivered production-facing batch ML workflows through Vertex AI Workbench and BigQuery, with measurable improvements in forecast accuracy and retention targeting.” This remains supported by the CV and more clearly communicates the type of production experience the candidate actually has.
3. In the Thistlebox experience section, identify the operational interfaces and ownership boundaries directly in the relevant bullets. Change the Cloud Run bullet to: “Built and containerised a Python Streamlit application and wrote the Dockerfile; the data platform team handled Cloud Run deployment. Used by approximately 25 people in product and growth.” This preserves the truthful distinction between creating the application and deploying it, which is important for a production-engineering role.
4. In the Additional Project section, change the heading “ADDITIONAL PROJECT” to “ADDITIONAL PROJECTS AND TRAINING” and retain the phrase “learning project only” in the image-classification entry. This prevents the PyTorch project from being misread as production AI experience while keeping the keyword searchable.

MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
5. In the Technical Skills section, change “Engineering and experimentation: pytest, unit testing, Docker, Streamlit, statsmodels, R Markdown, sequential A/B testing” to “Testing and engineering: pytest, unit testing, approximately 60% test coverage, Docker, Streamlit” and add a separate line “Statistics and experimentation: statsmodels, R Markdown, sequential A/B testing.” The 60% figure is already supported by the experience section and can strengthen keyword and impact scanning when clearly labelled.
6. In the Education section, add the dissertation topic in the same format used elsewhere: “MSc in Statistics — Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models.” If available in the existing CV source, the institution and completion year could also be included; do not invent them. This would improve completeness without adding unsupported qualifications.
